Recorded 5 verified peer-reviewed sources:

- [W4400305946](https://doi.org/10.1111/dom.15730): meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (n=1101 prediabetes/T2D). Claim: IF reduced weight (-4.56 kg), HbA1c (-0.81%), fasting glucose (-0.36 mmol/L), total cholesterol and triglycerides. Limitation: pools prediabetes with T2D; mixed IF protocols and control/CR comparators.
- [W3098144176](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu12113530) (PROFAST): 12-week 5:2 fasting (600-650 kcal/day x2/week) in prediabetes lowered HbA1c 43 to 41 mmol/mol, p<0.001. Limitation: n=26 completers, no non-fasting control, concurrent probiotic randomization.
- [W4387263072](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu15194233): RCT (n=72) in impaired fasting glucose, TRE +/- behavioral-economics vs usual care. Claim: no significant ITT differences in weight, fasting glucose, HbA1c, fasting insulin, lipids; benefit only in per-protocol compliers. Limitation: small, 3-arm, adherence-sensitive, surrogate outcomes.
- [W4387491927](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.advnut.2023.10.003): meta-analysis of 28 RCTs, intermittent vs continuous energy restriction. Claim: comparable weight (WMD -0.42 kg, p=0.132) and fat-mass change; slightly greater waist/FFM reduction with intermittent. Limitation: healthy adults, not prediabetes-specific; only 17/28 trials energy-matched.
- [W3194089427](https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2021.683140): TRE review. Claim: lower fasting/postprandial/24-h glucose, lower fasting insulin and improved insulin sensitivity in a range of trials, but a number of studies found adverse or no glycemic/lipid effects. Limitation: narrative review, heterogeneous windows and populations.

What this establishes: human RCT evidence is consistent with modest glycemic improvement (fasting glucose, HbA1c, fasting insulin/insulin sensitivity) under IF/TRE in at-risk adults, including prediabetes subgroups.

What it does not establish: whether IF improves insulin sensitivity per se beyond weight loss or beyond continuous calorie restriction — head-to-head meta-analytic evidence shows comparable weight effects, and the one IFG RCT was null by ITT. Clamp- or Matsuda-specific prediabetes effects, durability, and diabetes-incidence prevention are not established by these sources.

Gaps: no large long-term prediabetes-only RCT with gold-standard insulin sensitivity (clamp/Matsuda) and adherence-adjusted analysis; heterogeneity of fasting windows (early TRE vs 5:2 vs ADF) unresolved; arXiv search returned no usable preprints.
